rmfSteps.title: Step 0: Prepare
rmfSteps.summary: Establish organizational & system-level governance, assign AO/ISSM/ISSO and independent SCA, register system, and define authorization boundary before selecting controls.

rmfSteps.title: Step 1: Categorize
rmfSteps.summary: Map system data types against SP 800-60/CUI/privacy rules, rate Confidentiality/Integrity/Availability (LOW/MODERATE/HIGH), and compute High-Water Mark max(C, I, A).

rmfSteps.title: Step 2: Select
rmfSteps.summary: Select the SP 800-53B baseline matching categorization, apply FedRAMP/privacy/overlay rules, assign ODPs, and allocate controls as system-specific, inherited, or hybrid.

rmfSteps.title: Step 3: Implement
rmfSteps.summary: Implement controls consistently with enterprise architecture, harden endpoints/cloud infrastructure, eliminate 'TBD' placeholders, and document actual implementation statements in SSP.

rmfSteps.title: Step 4: Assess
rmfSteps.summary: Independent assessor/3PAO executes Examine, Interview, and Test procedures per SP 800-53A against actual evidence to determine control effectiveness and draft SAR.

rmfSteps.title: Step 5: Authorize
deliverables: Authorization Decision Letter (ATO / ATO w/ Conditions / DATO)
rmfSteps.summary: Authorizing Official reviews SSP, SAR, POA&M, and residual risk; only the AO renders formal ATO, conditional ATO, or Denial of Authorization (DATO).

rmfSteps.title: Step 6: Monitor
rmfSteps.summary: Maintain continuous visibility: monthly authenticated RA-5 scans, weekly AU-6 log analysis, strict POA&M SLA closure (High 30d / Mod 90d / Low 180d), and CISA KEV mitigation.

fips199Types.name: Personally Identifiable Information (PII)
fips199Types.notes: Typically triggers Privacy baseline + SP 800-122 protections.

fips199Types.name: Protected Health Information (PHI / HIPAA)
fips199Types.notes: High sensitivity for patient safety & HIPAA Privacy/Security Rules.

fips199Types.name: Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI)
fips199Types.notes: 32 CFR Part 2002 requires >= MODERATE Confidentiality; invokes NIST SP 800-171 for nonfederal systems.

fips199Types.name: ITAR / Export Controlled Technical Data
fips199Types.notes: Mandates HIGH Confidentiality under CNSSI 1253 / DoD IL5 overlays.

fips199Types.name: Federal Financial / Payment Transactions
fips199Types.notes: High integrity requirement against unauthorized ledger manipulation.

fips199Types.name: Critical Operational Telemetry / Emergency Response
fips199Types.notes: Loss or manipulation degrades safety-critical mission operations.

AC-2.low: Review accounts at least annually (ac-02_odp.10); notify account managers/ISSO within 24h when accounts are no longer required or users terminated/transferred.
AC-2.moderate: Review accounts monthly for privileged access and every 6 months for non-privileged access (ac-02_odp.10); notify within 24h when no longer required (ac-02_odp.06) and 12h on termination/transfer (ac-02_odp.07); disable user accounts within 24h per AC-2(3).
AC-2.high: Review accounts monthly for privileged access and every 6 months for non-privileged access (ac-02_odp.10); notify account managers/designated roles within 24h when accounts are no longer required (ac-02_odp.06) and within 8h when users are terminated/transferred (ac-02_odp.07); disable separated user accounts within 24h per AC-2(3).
AC-2.sla: Program Guidance (non-statutory): High <= 30d, Mod <= 90d, Low <= 180d (subject to AO tailoring)

AC-2(3).low: Included in Moderate/High FedRAMP baselines (agency-tailored under Low).
AC-2(3).moderate: Disable accounts within 24 hours for user accounts when expired/no longer associated/violating policy (ac-02.03_odp.01), or after thirty-five (35) days of inactivity (ac-02.03_odp.02); CSP defines non-user/device periods approved by JAB/AO.
AC-2(3).high: Disable user accounts within 24 hours when expired, terminated/no longer associated, or violating policy (ac-02.03_odp.01), or after thirty-five (35) days of inactivity (ac-02.03_odp.02); CSP defines non-user/device timeframes approved by JAB/AO.
AC-2(3).sla: Program Guidance (non-statutory): High <= 30d (subject to AO tailoring)

AC-3.low: Enforce least-privilege RBAC and default-deny access policies.
AC-3.moderate: Enforce least-privilege RBAC, API authorization, and disallow console/IAM bypass.
AC-3.high: Enforce hardware-backed least-privilege RBAC, explicit-deny SCP/IAM guardrails, and zero console bypass.

AC-7.low: Lock account for 15 minutes or admin unlock after max 5 consecutive invalid login attempts in 15 minutes.
AC-7.moderate: Max 3 consecutive invalid login attempts during 15-minute interval; lock 15 minutes or until admin unlock.
AC-7.high: Max 3 consecutive invalid login attempts during 15-minute interval; lock >= 15 minutes or until admin unlock.

AC-11.low: Initiate session lock after 15 minutes of inactivity.
AC-11.moderate: Initiate device/session lock after <= 15 minutes of inactivity; conceal prior display.
AC-11.high: Initiate device/session lock after <= 15 minutes of inactivity and require re-authentication with MFA.

AC-12.low: Terminate network/UI sessions after defined inactivity period.
AC-12.moderate: Terminate interactive sessions after <= 30 minutes (privileged <= 15 minutes) of inactivity.
AC-12.high: Terminate sessions after <= 15 minutes (standard & privileged <= 15 minutes) of inactivity.

AU-2.low: Log authentication, account creation/deletion, privilege escalation, and policy changes.
AU-2.moderate: Capture auth, priv-esc, object access/deletion, admin commands, and config changes correlated centrally.
AU-2.high: Capture comprehensive immutable security/admin telemetry, command-level privileged actions, and tamper logs.

AU-6.low: Review and analyze system audit records at least weekly.
AU-6.moderate: Review/analyze audit records at least weekly (<= 7 days) and correlate automated SIEM alerts.
AU-6.high: Review/analyze audit records at least weekly (<= 7 days) with real-time SIEM correlation and automated alerting.

AU-11.low: Retain audit records at least 90 days online / 1 year archived.
AU-11.moderate: Retain audit records >= 90 days immediately searchable online and >= 1 year archived.
AU-11.high: Retain audit records >= 90 days hot online and >= 1 year WORM/immutable archive.

CA-7.low: Report ConMon metrics annually/monthly per FedRAMP PMO.
CA-7.moderate: Deliver monthly ConMon vulnerability scans, POA&M updates, and annual 3PAO subset assessment.
CA-7.high: Deliver monthly ConMon scans (OS, DB, Web/Container), real-time significant-change alerts, and annual 3PAO re-assessment.

CM-2.low: Maintain and review baseline configuration annually and upon significant change.
CM-2.moderate: Maintain version-controlled IaC/gold-image baseline configuration; review >= annually and after major change.
CM-2.high: Maintain signed, version-controlled baseline configuration (IaC/CIS/DISA STIG); review >= annually and on every significant change.

CM-6.low: Apply CIS Level 1 / DISA STIG baseline configurations; document approved deviations.
CM-6.moderate: Enforce CIS/DISA STIG configuration settings across OS, DB, containers, and cloud control planes.
CM-6.high: Enforce DISA STIG / CIS hardened configurations with automated drift detection and >= 95% compliance threshold.

IA-2.low: Uniquely identify and authenticate organizational users; MFA implementations must adhere to NIST SP 800-63B and be phishing-resistant (IA-2 FedRAMP Additional Requirements).
IA-2.moderate: Uniquely identify organizational users; adhere to NIST SP 800-63B Digital Identity Guidelines and enforce phishing-resistant MFA per Additional FedRAMP Requirements.
IA-2.high: Uniquely identify organizational users; adhere to NIST SP 800-63B Digital Identity Guidelines and enforce phishing-resistant MFA across privileged and non-privileged enhancements (IA-2 Additional FedRAMP Requirements).
IA-2.sla: Program Guidance (non-statutory): High <= 30d (subject to AO tailoring)

IA-2(1).low: Enforce phishing-resistant MFA for access to privileged accounts (not in Low baseline unless tailored; see IA-2(1) when applied).
IA-2(1).moderate: Implement phishing-resistant MFA for access to privileged accounts per SP 800-63-3 (63A/63B/63C). Guidance (ia-2.1_fr_gdn.1): MFA to subsequent components in the same user domain is not required.
IA-2(1).high: Implement phishing-resistant MFA for access to privileged accounts per SP 800-63-3 (63A/63B/63C). Guidance (ia-2.1_fr_gdn.1): MFA to subsequent components in the same user domain is not required (evaluate full end-to-end auth path including bastion/IdP).
IA-2(1).sla: Program Guidance (non-statutory): High <= 30d (subject to AO tailoring)

IA-2(2).low: Phishing-resistant MFA for access to non-privileged accounts (when included/tailored).
IA-2(2).moderate: Phishing-resistant MFA for non-privileged accounts per SP 800-63-3; subsequent same-domain components exempt per ia-2.2_fr_gdn.1.
IA-2(2).high: Phishing-resistant MFA for non-privileged accounts per SP 800-63-3; subsequent same-domain components exempt per ia-2.2_fr_gdn.1.

IA-2(6).moderate: Implement MFA for local, network, and remote access (ia-02.06_odp.01) to privileged and non-privileged accounts (ia-02.06_odp.02) using a separate device meeting FIPS-validated or NSA-approved cryptography (ia-02.06_odp.03; e.g., PIV/SP 800-157 or FIDO2).
IA-2(6).high: Implement MFA for local, network, and remote access (ia-02.06_odp.01) to privileged and non-privileged accounts (ia-02.06_odp.02) using a separate device meeting FIPS-validated or NSA-approved cryptography (ia-02.06_odp.03); evaluate end-to-end SSH/bastion/IdP auth path.
IA-2(6).sla: Program Guidance (non-statutory): High <= 30d (subject to AO tailoring)

RA-5.low: Monthly OS scans (ra-5_prm_1); remediate High <= 30d, Moderate <= 90d, Low <= 180d from discovery (ra-05_odp.03); CISA KEV catalog dates supersede RA-5(d) timelines where applicable.
RA-5.moderate: Monthly OS/infrastructure, web app/API, and database scans (ra-5_prm_1) + annual 3PAO scan; mitigate High <= 30d, Moderate <= 90d, Low <= 180d (ra-05_odp.03); CISA KEV catalog dates supersede where listed.
RA-5.high: Monthly OS/infrastructure, web app/API, and database scans (ra-5_prm_1) + annual 3PAO scan; mitigate High <= 30d, Moderate <= 90d, Low <= 180d (ra-05_odp.03); CISA KEV catalog dates supersede for KEV-listed CVEs only.
RA-5.sla: Scan <= 30d; RA-5(d) ODP: High 30d, Mod 90d, Low 180d (KEV supersedes for listed CVEs)

SI-2.low: Install security-relevant software and firmware updates within thirty (30) days of release of updates (si-02_odp).
SI-2.moderate: Install security-relevant software and firmware updates within thirty (30) days of release of updates (si-02_odp).
SI-2.high: Install security-relevant software and firmware updates within thirty (30) days of release of updates (si-02_odp); CISA BOD 22-01 applies specifically to CISA KEV-listed vulnerabilities.
SI-2.sla: SI-2(c) ODP: <= 30d of update release (program POA&M / BOD 22-01 KEV-scoped)

GV.OC.title: Organizational Context

GV.OC-01.title: GV.OC-01
GV.OC-01.statement: The organizational mission is understood and informs cybersecurity risk management

GV.OC-02.title: GV.OC-02
GV.OC-02.statement: Internal and external stakeholders are understood, and their needs and expectations regarding cybersecurity risk management are understood and considered

GV.OC-03.title: GV.OC-03
GV.OC-03.statement: Legal, regulatory, and contractual requirements regarding cybersecurity - including privacy and civil liberties obligations - are understood and managed

GV.OC-04.title: GV.OC-04
GV.OC-04.statement: Critical objectives, capabilities, and services that external stakeholders depend on or expect from the organization are understood and communicated

GV.OC-05.title: GV.OC-05
GV.OC-05.statement: Outcomes, capabilities, and services that the organization depends on are understood and communicated

GV.OV.statement: Results of organization-wide cybersecurity risk management activities and performance are used to inform, improve, and adjust the risk management strategy

GV.OV-01.title: GV.OV-01
GV.OV-01.statement: Cybersecurity risk management strategy outcomes are reviewed to inform and adjust strategy and direction

GV.OV-02.title: GV.OV-02
GV.OV-02.statement: The cybersecurity risk management strategy is reviewed and adjusted to ensure coverage of organizational requirements and risks

GV.OV-03.title: GV.OV-03

GV.PO.title: Policy

GV.PO-01.title: GV.PO-01
GV.PO-01.statement: Policy for managing cybersecurity risks is established based on organizational context, cybersecurity strategy, and priorities and is communicated and enforced

GV.PO-02.title: GV.PO-02

GV.RM.title: Risk Management Strategy

GV.RM-01.statement: Risk management objectives are established and agreed to by organizational stakeholders

GV.RM-02.title: GV.RM-02

GV.RM-03.title: GV.RM-03

GV.RM-04.title: GV.RM-04
GV.RM-04.statement: Strategic direction that describes appropriate risk response options is established and communicated

GV.RM-05.title: GV.RM-05
GV.RM-05.statement: Lines of communication across the organization are established for cybersecurity risks, including risks from suppliers and other third parties

GV.RM-06.title: GV.RM-06
GV.RM-06.statement: A standardized method for calculating, documenting, categorizing, and prioritizing cybersecurity risks is established and communicated

GV.RM-07.title: GV.RM-07
GV.RM-07.statement: Strategic opportunities (i.e., positive risks) are characterized and are included in organizational cybersecurity risk discussions

GV.RR.title: Roles, Responsibilities, and Authorities

GV.RR-01.statement: Organizational leadership is responsible and accountable for cybersecurity risk and fosters a culture that is risk-aware, ethical, and continually improving

GV.RR-02.title: GV.RR-02
GV.RR-02.statement: Roles, responsibilities, and authorities related to cybersecurity risk management are established, communicated, understood, and enforced

GV.RR-03.title: GV.RR-03
GV.RR-03.statement: Adequate resources are allocated commensurate with the cybersecurity risk strategy, roles, responsibilities, and policies

GV.RR-04.title: GV.RR-04
GV.RR-04.statement: Cybersecurity is included in human resources practices

GV.SC-01.statement: A cybersecurity supply chain risk management program, strategy, objectives, policies, and processes are established and agreed to by organizational stakeholders

GV.SC-02.title: GV.SC-02
GV.SC-02.statement: Cybersecurity roles and responsibilities for suppliers, customers, and partners are established, communicated, and coordinated internally and externally

GV.SC-04.statement: Suppliers are known and prioritized by criticality

GV.SC-08.statement: Relevant suppliers and other third parties are included in incident planning, response, and recovery activities

GV.SC-09.title: GV.SC-09
GV.SC-09.statement: Supply chain security practices are integrated into cybersecurity and enterprise risk management programs, and their performance is monitored throughout the technology product and service life cycle

GV.SC-10.title: GV.SC-10

ID.AM-07.title: ID.AM-07

ID.AM-08.title: ID.AM-08
ID.AM-08.statement: Systems, hardware, software, services, and data are managed throughout their life cycles

ID.BE-02.title: ID.BE-02
ID.BE-02.statement: The organization’s place in critical infrastructure and its industry sector is identified and communicated

ID.BE-03.title: ID.BE-03
ID.BE-03.statement: Priorities for organizational mission, objectives, and activities are established and communicated

ID.BE-04.title: ID.BE-04
ID.BE-04.statement: Dependencies and critical functions for delivery of critical services are established

ID.BE-05.title: ID.BE-05
ID.BE-05.statement: Resilience requirements to support delivery of critical services are established for all operating states (e.g. under duress/attack, during recovery, normal operations)

ID.GV-01.statement: Organizational cybersecurity policy is established and communicated

ID.GV-02.title: ID.GV-02
ID.GV-02.statement: Cybersecurity roles and responsibilities are coordinated and aligned with internal roles and external partners

ID.GV-03.title: ID.GV-03
ID.GV-03.statement: Legal and regulatory requirements regarding cybersecurity, including privacy and civil liberties obligations, are understood and managed

ID.GV-04.title: ID.GV-04
ID.GV-04.statement: Governance and risk management processes address cybersecurity risks

ID.IM-02.statement: Improvements are identified from security tests and exercises, including those done in coordination with suppliers and relevant third parties

ID.IM-03.title: ID.IM-03
ID.IM-03.statement: Improvements are identified from execution of operational processes, procedures, and activities

ID.IM-04.title: ID.IM-04
ID.IM-04.statement: Incident response plans and other cybersecurity plans that affect operations are established, communicated, maintained, and improved

ID.RA-01.statement: Vulnerabilities in assets are identified, validated, and recorded

ID.RA-02.title: ID.RA-02
ID.RA-02.statement: Cyber threat intelligence is received from information sharing forums and sources

ID.RA-03.title: ID.RA-03
ID.RA-03.statement: Internal and external threats to the organization are identified and recorded

ID.RA-04.title: ID.RA-04
ID.RA-04.statement: Potential impacts and likelihoods of threats exploiting vulnerabilities are identified and recorded

ID.RA-05.title: ID.RA-05
ID.RA-05.statement: Threats, vulnerabilities, likelihoods, and impacts are used to understand inherent risk and inform risk response prioritization

ID.RA-06.title: ID.RA-06

ID.RA-07.title: ID.RA-07

ID.RA-08.title: ID.RA-08

ID.RA-09.title: ID.RA-09

ID.RA-10.title: ID.RA-10

ID.RM-01.title: ID.RM-01
ID.RM-01.statement: Risk management processes are established, managed, and agreed to by organizational stakeholders

ID.RM-02.title: ID.RM-02

ID.RM-03.title: ID.RM-03
ID.RM-03.statement: The organization’s determination of risk tolerance is informed by its role in critical infrastructure and sector specific risk analysis

ID.SC-01.title: ID.SC-01

ID.SC-04.title: ID.SC-04
ID.SC-04.statement: Suppliers and third-party partners are routinely assessed using audits, test results, or other forms of evaluations to confirm they are meeting their contractual obligations.

ID.SC-05.title: ID.SC-05
ID.SC-05.statement: Response and recovery planning and testing are conducted with suppliers and third-party providers

PR.AA-01.statement: Identities and credentials for authorized users, services, and hardware are managed by the organization

PR.AA-02.statement: Identities are proofed and bound to credentials based on the context of interactions

PR.AA-03.title: PR.AA-03
PR.AA-03.statement: Users, services, and hardware are authenticated

PR.AA-04.title: PR.AA-04
PR.AA-04.statement: Identity assertions are protected, conveyed, and verified

PR.AA-05.title: PR.AA-05

PR.AA-06.title: PR.AA-06

PR.AC.title: Identity Management, Authentication and Access Control

PR.AT-02.title: PR.AT-02

PR.AT-03.title: PR.AT-03

PR.AT-04.title: PR.AT-04

PR.AT-05.title: PR.AT-05
PR.AT-05.statement: Physical and cybersecurity personnel understand their roles and responsibilities

PR.DS-04.title: PR.DS-04

PR.DS-06.title: PR.DS-06

PR.DS-07.title: PR.DS-07
PR.DS-07.statement: The development and testing environment(s) are separate from the production environment

PR.DS-08.title: PR.DS-08
PR.DS-08.statement: Integrity checking mechanisms are used to verify hardware integrity

PR.DS-10.title: PR.DS-10

PR.DS-11.title: PR.DS-11
PR.DS-11.statement: Backups of data are created, protected, maintained, and tested

PR.IP-01.title: PR.IP-01

PR.IP-02.title: PR.IP-02

PR.IP-03.title: PR.IP-03

PR.IP-04.title: PR.IP-04
PR.IP-04.statement: Backups of information are conducted, maintained, and tested

PR.IP-05.title: PR.IP-05
PR.IP-05.statement: Policy and regulations regarding the physical operating environment for organizational assets are met

PR.IP-06.title: PR.IP-06
PR.IP-06.statement: Data is destroyed according to policy

PR.IP-08.title: PR.IP-08
PR.IP-08.statement: Effectiveness of protection technologies is shared

PR.IP-09.title: PR.IP-09

PR.IP-10.title: PR.IP-10

PR.IP-11.title: PR.IP-11
PR.IP-11.statement: Cybersecurity is included in human resources practices (e.g., deprovisioning, personnel screening)

PR.IP-12.title: PR.IP-12

PR.IR-03.title: PR.IR-03

PR.IR-04.title: PR.IR-04
PR.IR-04.statement: Adequate resource capacity to ensure availability is maintained

PR.MA-01.title: PR.MA-01
PR.MA-01.statement: Maintenance and repair of organizational assets are performed and logged, with approved and controlled tools

PR.MA-02.title: PR.MA-02
PR.MA-02.statement: Remote maintenance of organizational assets is approved, logged, and performed in a manner that prevents unauthorized access

PR.PS.title: Platform Security
PR.PS.statement: The hardware, software (e.g., firmware, operating systems, applications), and services of physical and virtual platforms are managed consistent with the organization's risk strategy to protect their confidentiality, integrity, and…

PR.PS-01.title: PR.PS-01
PR.PS-01.statement: Configuration management practices are established and applied

PR.PS-02.title: PR.PS-02
PR.PS-02.statement: Software is maintained, replaced, and removed commensurate with risk

PR.PS-03.title: PR.PS-03
PR.PS-03.statement: Hardware is maintained, replaced, and removed commensurate with risk

PR.PS-04.title: PR.PS-04
PR.PS-04.statement: Log records are generated and made available for continuous monitoring

PR.PS-05.title: PR.PS-05
PR.PS-05.statement: Installation and execution of unauthorized software are prevented

PR.PS-06.title: PR.PS-06
PR.PS-06.statement: Secure software development practices are integrated, and their performance is monitored throughout the software development life cycle

PR.PT-01.title: PR.PT-01
PR.PT-01.statement: Audit/log records are determined, documented, implemented, and reviewed in accordance with policy

PR.PT-02.title: PR.PT-02
PR.PT-02.statement: Removable media is protected and its use restricted according to policy

PR.PT-03.title: PR.PT-03
PR.PT-03.statement: The principle of least functionality is incorporated by configuring systems to provide only essential capabilities

PR.PT-04.title: PR.PT-04
PR.PT-04.statement: Communications and control networks are protected

PR.PT-05.title: PR.PT-05
PR.PT-05.statement: Mechanisms (e.g., failsafe, load balancing, hot swap) are implemented to achieve resilience requirements in normal and adverse situations

DE.AE.title: Adverse Event Analysis
DE.AE.statement: Anomalies, indicators of compromise, and other potentially adverse events are analyzed to characterize the events and detect cybersecurity incidents

DE.AE-01.title: DE.AE-01
DE.AE-01.statement: A baseline of network operations and expected data flows for users and systems is established and managed

DE.AE-02.title: DE.AE-02
DE.AE-02.statement: Potentially adverse events are analyzed to better understand associated activities

DE.AE-03.title: DE.AE-03
DE.AE-03.statement: Information is correlated from multiple sources

DE.AE-04.title: DE.AE-04
DE.AE-04.statement: The estimated impact and scope of adverse events are understood

DE.AE-06.title: DE.AE-06
DE.AE-06.statement: Information on adverse events is provided to authorized staff and tools

DE.AE-07.title: DE.AE-07
DE.AE-07.statement: Cyber threat intelligence and other contextual information are integrated into the analysis

DE.AE-08.title: DE.AE-08
DE.AE-08.statement: Incidents are declared when adverse events meet the defined incident criteria

DE.CM.title: Continuous Monitoring
DE.CM.statement: Assets are monitored to find anomalies, indicators of compromise, and other potentially adverse events

DE.CM-01.title: DE.CM-01
DE.CM-01.statement: Networks and network services are monitored to find potentially adverse events

DE.CM-02.title: DE.CM-02
DE.CM-02.statement: The physical environment is monitored to find potentially adverse events

DE.CM-03.title: DE.CM-03
DE.CM-03.statement: Personnel activity and technology usage are monitored to find potentially adverse events

DE.CM-06.title: DE.CM-06
DE.CM-06.statement: External service provider activities and services are monitored to find potentially adverse events

DE.CM-07.title: DE.CM-07
DE.CM-07.statement: Monitoring for unauthorized personnel, connections, devices, and software is performed

DE.CM-09.title: DE.CM-09
DE.CM-09.statement: Computing hardware and software, runtime environments, and their data are monitored to find potentially adverse events

DE.DP-01.title: DE.DP-01
DE.DP-01.statement: Roles and responsibilities for detection are well defined to ensure accountability

DE.DP-02.title: DE.DP-02
DE.DP-02.statement: Detection activities comply with all applicable requirements

RS.AN.title: Incident Analysis
RS.AN.statement: Investigations are conducted to ensure effective response and support forensics and recovery activities

RS.AN-01.title: RS.AN-01
RS.AN-01.statement: Notifications from detection systems are investigated

RS.AN-02.title: RS.AN-02
RS.AN-02.statement: The impact of the incident is understood

RS.AN-03.title: RS.AN-03
RS.AN-03.statement: Analysis is performed to establish what has taken place during an incident and the root cause of the incident

RS.AN-04.title: RS.AN-04
RS.AN-04.statement: Incidents are categorized consistent with response plans

RS.AN-05.title: RS.AN-05
RS.AN-05.statement: Processes are established to receive, analyze and respond to vulnerabilities disclosed to the organization from internal and external sources (e.g. internal testing, security bulletins, or security researchers)

RS.AN-06.title: RS.AN-06
RS.AN-06.statement: Actions performed during an investigation are recorded, and the records' integrity and provenance are preserved

RS.AN-07.title: RS.AN-07
RS.AN-07.statement: Incident data and metadata are collected, and their integrity and provenance are preserved

RS.AN-08.title: RS.AN-08
RS.AN-08.statement: An incident's magnitude is estimated and validated

RS.CO.title: Incident Response Reporting and Communication
RS.CO.statement: Response activities are coordinated with internal and external stakeholders as required by laws, regulations, or policies

RS.CO-01.title: RS.CO-01
RS.CO-01.statement: Personnel know their roles and order of operations when a response is needed

RS.CO-02.title: RS.CO-02
RS.CO-02.statement: Internal and external stakeholders are notified of incidents

RS.CO-03.title: RS.CO-03
RS.CO-03.statement: Information is shared with designated internal and external stakeholders

RS.CO-04.title: RS.CO-04
RS.CO-04.statement: Coordination with stakeholders occurs consistent with response plans

RS.CO-05.title: RS.CO-05
RS.CO-05.statement: Voluntary information sharing occurs with external stakeholders to achieve broader cybersecurity situational awareness

RS.MA.title: Incident Management
RS.MA.statement: Responses to detected cybersecurity incidents are managed

RS.MA-01.title: RS.MA-01
RS.MA-01.statement: The incident response plan is executed in coordination with relevant third parties once an incident is declared

RS.MA-02.title: RS.MA-02
RS.MA-02.statement: Incident reports are triaged and validated

RS.MA-04.title: RS.MA-04
RS.MA-04.statement: Incidents are escalated or elevated as needed

RS.MA-05.title: RS.MA-05
RS.MA-05.statement: The criteria for initiating incident recovery are applied

RS.MI.title: Incident Mitigation
RS.MI.statement: Activities are performed to prevent expansion of an event and mitigate its effects

RS.MI-03.title: RS.MI-03
RS.MI-03.statement: Newly identified vulnerabilities are mitigated or documented as accepted risks

RS.RP-01.title: RS.RP-01
RS.RP-01.statement: Response plan is executed during or after an incident

RC.CO.title: Incident Recovery Communication
RC.CO.statement: Restoration activities are coordinated with internal and external parties

RC.CO-02.title: RC.CO-02
RC.CO-02.statement: Reputation is repaired after an incident

RC.CO-03.title: RC.CO-03
RC.CO-03.statement: Recovery activities and progress in restoring operational capabilities are communicated to designated internal and external stakeholders

RC.CO-04.title: RC.CO-04
RC.CO-04.statement: Public updates on incident recovery are shared using approved methods and messaging

RC.RP.title: Incident Recovery Plan Execution
RC.RP.statement: Restoration activities are performed to ensure operational availability of systems and services affected by cybersecurity incidents

RC.RP-01.title: RC.RP-01
RC.RP-01.statement: The recovery portion of the incident response plan is executed once initiated from the incident response process

RC.RP-02.title: RC.RP-02
RC.RP-02.statement: Recovery actions are selected, scoped, prioritized, and performed

RC.RP-03.title: RC.RP-03
RC.RP-03.statement: The integrity of backups and other restoration assets is verified before using them for restoration

RC.RP-04.title: RC.RP-04
RC.RP-04.statement: Critical mission functions and cybersecurity risk management are considered to establish post-incident operational norms

RC.RP-05.title: RC.RP-05
RC.RP-05.statement: The integrity of restored assets is verified, systems and services are restored, and normal operating status is confirmed

RC.RP-06.title: RC.RP-06
RC.RP-06.statement: The end of incident recovery is declared based on criteria, and incident-related documentation is completed
